body:
[P2] Keep an already presented scratchpad read valid when a write arrives

In EX_WAIT with the current tag and ex_read_busy=0, set ex_rd_valid=1, ex_wr_valid=0 and sp_rd_ready=0. Lines 102–103 present sp_rd_valid=1 and ex_rd_ready=0. On the next cycle, keep the read valid/address/tag stable and assert ex_wr_valid on the independent write channel. current_read becomes 0 solely because of !ex_wr_valid, so sp_rd_valid drops before the read handshake. Both kernel channels can obey the documented hold-until-accepted rule, but the controller violates that same rule on its scratchpad channel.

The README grants write priority over a newly presented read; that must not preempt a read already held under backpressure. Latch/retain the read grant until acceptance, then keep writes blocked until its response drains. Add a directed case that stalls a presented read and subsequently presents a current-tag write while the read stays asserted; check stable scratchpad valid/address/tag and read-before-write completion. The existing event replay chooses either a read or a write at a time (tb_engine.v:333–342), so its held-read assertion never encounters this case.
